A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Token Bottleneck (ToBo). All 17 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Relocated analyses can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated and physical robot experiments, video label propagation results, scalability experiments, and a masking-ratio ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds bottleneck and temporal ablations plus computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The single-token pipeline, decoder, and cosine reconstruction objective in Section 3.3 remain unchanged. Appendix C.1 newly states that training uses an auxiliary Siamese masked-autoencoding loss, but does not establish whether this changes training or discloses an existing component. An actual objective change cannot be determined reliably.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain Kinetics-400, Franka Kitchen, CortexBench, RLBench, the three physical robot tasks, DAVIS, VIP, and JHMDB. New ablations vary training configurations within this coverage. Both masking-ratio plots already show five Kitchen tasks; changing the accompanying text from three to five corrects the description.

E2.justification: Baseline membership in corresponding comparisons is unchanged. CLIP, DINOv2, SigLIP, and SigLIP2 already appeared in v1 Appendix A.1, now moved to Section 5. The new diagnostic comparisons reuse MAE, SiamMAE, and RSP.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols remain intact. New Appendix A experiments use ViT-B/16 trained for 100 epochs and vary token count, maximum temporal gap, identical source/target frames, and four source frames. Section 5 also introduces training/inference FLOP evaluation with matched backbone and input-resolution controls.

E4.justification: New Appendix A and Table A directly test bottleneck capacity, temporal-gap sensitivity, the necessity of temporal differences, and multiple source frames. These substantially expand evidence about central design choices beyond v1's masking-ratio ablation. Section 5 also adds an efficiency analysis; the existing masking analysis and robot trajectories are retained.

E5.justification: The reported seed counts, 95% confidence intervals, and three-seed scalability means and standard deviations are retained. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure is specified for the added ablations. Revised numerical uncertainty values belong to E6.

E6.justification: Table A adds substantial ablation results, including reported mean success rates of 61.1% for default ToBo, 53.5% without temporal differences, and 46.9% with multiple source frames. Table 9 adds training costs of 15.9 GFLOPs for ToBo versus 32.5 for RSP. Retained results also change: Knob1 on becomes 57.0±2.0 from 57.3±2.3, DMC becomes 73.5±0.9 from 73.5±8.6, and aggregate Kitchen performance becomes 68.0 from 68.1 in the robot-representation comparison. The relocated vision-language table updates Knob1 and its gain accordingly.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, masking formulation, and reconstruction-loss equation are retained. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs, and the added explanations and empirical ablations introduce no new derivations.

C1.justification: The central representation-learning, downstream-performance, transfer, and scalability claims remain. v2 adds computational overhead of multi-objective frameworks to the conclusion's motivation, giving computational efficiency a more explicit role in the paper's contribution framing.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds interpretations concerning excessive bottleneck capacity, short versus long temporal gaps, lost temporal supervision with identical frames, and the cost and underperformance of a naive multi-frame extension. Section 5 adds an efficiency-performance interpretation. These extend the retained summarization and temporal-learning explanation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access statement in the abstract, discloses the auxiliary Siamese masked-autoencoding loss in Appendix C.1, and specifies the new ablation configurations. Conversely, Tables 1–3 remove explicit footnotes identifying baseline results taken from Jang et al. Most existing implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the citation 'Morphing tokens draw strong masked image models' and removes the separate Kinetics-700, Something-Something, and Ego4D references. Section 3.2 also expands positioning against RSP's computational cost and patch-correspondence approaches, while retaining the broader related-work framework.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 is locally rewritten and expanded, 'expansion' becomes 'reconstruction,' and the vision-language comparison and masking analysis move from Appendix A into Section 5. The discussion is reordered and Appendix A receives new analyses, while most existing prose and the overall section structure remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds the FLOP table and four-panel ablation table, relocates the vision-language table and masking plot into the main text, and reorders existing tables. Figures 1 and 3 receive illustrative edits, and the environment montage is enlarged and relocated. Existing experimental photographs and masking curves are retained.

improvement.justification: The new ablations directly support previously untested aspects of the single-token design and temporal supervision, while Table 9 provides useful computational-cost evidence. The code pointer and added loss disclosure improve reproducibility information. These gains outweigh the removal of explicit baseline-source footnotes, although the auxiliary loss remains incompletely specified and its relationship to the unchanged main objective is unclear.
